visualReview.method: contact sheets (16:9, 9:16, 1:1, alternative, long-labels, es) and dense frame strips viewed as images; no real-time playback
findings: Round-4 FAIL (1:1 fill) fixed: 1:1 recomposed with each board flanked by two narrow bookcases; at 1080x1080 the default final spans about x 69-1011 (87% of the frame, about 99% of the caption-safe width) and fills the caption-safe box vertically (y about 67-859, with the bottom caption band kept free). This is a real square re-layout, not the 16:9 design shrunk, and it compares well with accepted reference LAW-0443 1:1

Round-4 FAIL (tiny key labels in 1:1) fixed, measured myself with getScreenCTM at 1080: state tags 'Exact words copied' / 'Interpretation by R. Ferrer' 18.0 px, guide chips 18.0 px, strip and page passages 15.2 px, card body 15.5 px, A/B subtitles 15.3 px, A/B titles 27.3 px, disclaimer 20.1 px

1:1 storyboard checked in dense strips (0.34-0.66 and 0.70-1.0): A's copied strip slides out from beneath the page (the page covers it correctly). B's card slides sideways out from behind the right commentaries bookcase, and a highlighted volume shows on the matching row. There is no teleport. The 'Same facts' chip fades out (0.78-0.84) before 'Changed fact' and 'Two side notes' fade in (0.87+), so there is no garbled cross-fade. The guide draws down from A's strip and lands on the top edge of B's card, next to the push pin. The dotted leader from the 'Changed fact' chip reaches the bottom of B's card and runs right of the B tag

No state shown too early: at t=0.1 both boards are identical with no strip or card, and the parallel marks appear at the change beat. Labels-hidden 1:1 strip: the action (strip from the page, card from the bookcase, thread) reads without text

Presets in 1:1: baseline-es text fits, and contrast-or-alternative (passage 4 of 4) keeps the strip, card, tags and the 'Changed fact' chip clear of the board frames and of each other. long-labels-stress keeps a 2-line strip, 2-line tag and 2-line bottom chip with no truncation or collision. Charcoal background with the slate palette renders cleanly

16:9 and 9:16 dense strips re-checked: unchanged and still at reference quality (the card drops from the shelf, and the guide runs in a side lane). automated.json: all checks pass, warnings [] (no text-overlap or low-frame-coverage), no console errors, no external requests

Non-blocking: long-labels-stress 1:1 is height-limited, with strip text 12.8 px and tag and guide chips 15.2 px. That is comparable to the accepted 16:9 long-labels (strip 15.2, tags 14.6-16.6). The copied strip's words sit only about 3 px from its left and top edges in every ratio, which reads as a cut-out quote but could use 2-4 units more inner padding

Four treatments remain distinct: 0061 is a story (a researcher at a catalogue search and bookcase pins the note beside the text), 0062 is a mechanism (an anatomy of the search, shelves and relations), 0063 is a contrast (two complete boards: copied words vs attributed reading), and 0064 is an inspect (a lens isolates the pinpoint, which is changed from paragraph 2 to paragraph 3 and then returns). Their renders are unchanged since acceptance per accept.mjs

Legal content: the code, rule and commentators are fictional and the jurisdiction is unspecified. The interpretation is attributed to a fictional commentator and not stated as law. The closing chip says neither note is ranked or preferred, and there is no verdict

contentReview.scope: Illustrative labelling, fictional data, no legal conclusion/verdict/ranking in the rendered scene. Not a legal verification.
